title: Charlie Calloway's fight in Atlanta
summary: Punch recounts a show MC beating a white drunk and getting away.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well did any of the guys you know ever get in serious trouble, say, you know, down

behind the sun as we say? No, one boy named Charlie Calloway, we was playing, I was playing with the same shooting, this happened in Atlanta, Georgia, was it? Yeah, Atlanta, Georgia. And the white guy was drunk, you know, he kept on buying him, kept on buying him, he was selling Coca-Cola, you know, around him, and all the white folks, he didn't keep on following the boy around. Who was selling Coke all the time? Charlie Calloway, colored boy, he was the MC on the show, but before the show go on, you know, to sell Coke and candy and all that. And he said, well he just kept on until he got married every hard way and hit the boy. So the boy just jumped on him and whipped him. Just whipped him up good. Well nobody said a word. And when the law comes, they take Charlie Calloway, all the white folks got up to him, you know, that boy was right. So the men kept on buying him, kept on wood, and peeking at him all the time. Calloway whipped the white guy. Yeah, whipped him up good. And he didn't bother Calloway, told him to go on and go to the white, took him and made the white man get away with him. Didn't come to jail, but he made him get away from around there. But he was really wrong, that fellow was. He just kept on after that. Say, remember that Blue Island Blues you made
